audits.title: Audit of thrombolysis initiated in an accident and emergency department.
audits.standard: Early thrombolysis after acute myocardial infarction; door to needle and pain to needle times
audits.setting: Accident and emergency department and coronary care unit (about 5 km away), district general hospital, Stockport

cycle1.result: Group 1 (thrombolysis in CCU): geometric mean door to needle 128 min, pain to needle 242 min.

audits.intervention: Selected patients given thrombolysis in the A and E department before transfer, after oral confirmation of myocardial infarction by the CCU admitting officer on receipt of a faxed ECG.

cycle2.period: Six months from start of new procedure (prospective)
cycle2.result: Group 2b (thrombolysis in A and E): geometric mean door to needle 38 min and pain to needle 141 min, v 121 min and 237 min in ineligible patients treated in CCU (group 2a, n=30); both p < 0.0001.

audits.other_findings: Adverse effects did not differ significantly. Nine deaths (six in group 1, three in group 2b), in-hospital mortality 9.9%.
audits.citation: Nee PA, Gray AJ, Martin MA. Audit of thrombolysis initiated in an accident and emergency department. Qual Health Care. 1994;3(1):29-33. doi:10.1136/qshc.3.1.29. PMID: 10136256.

audits.title: An audit of clinical nurse practitioner led thrombolysis to improve the treatment of acute myocardial infarction.
audits.standard: Acceptable door to needle times for thrombolysis in AMI
audits.setting: William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital, Ashford, Kent

cycle1.result: Median door to needle time 60 min (range 42-110 min).

audits.intervention: Cardiac nurse practitioner led intravenous thrombolysis.

cycle2.result: Median door to needle time 30 min (range 20-61 min).

audits.other_findings: 151 consecutive patients (163 thrombolysis episodes) across both periods; nurse-led thrombolysis judged safe.
audits.citation: Lloyd G, Roberts A, Bashir I, Mumby M, Kamalvand K, Cooke R. An audit of clinical nurse practitioner led thrombolysis to improve the treatment of acute myocardial infarction. J Public Health Med. 2000;22(4):462-465. doi:10.1093/pubmed/22.4.462. PMID: 11192272.

audits.title: Improving care for patients with acute coronary syndromes: initial results from the National Audit of Myocardial Infarction Project (MINAP).

cycle1.result: Median arrival to treatment 38 minutes (IQR 22-58); treatment within 2 hours of symptom onset 32.5%.

audits.intervention: Electronic data entry system with contemporary online feedback and comparison with national performance

cycle2.result: Median arrival to treatment 20 minutes (IQR 14-28); 77.6% thrombolysed within 30 minutes by mid 2003; within 2 hours of onset 40.3%.

audits.citation: Birkhead JS, Walker L, Pearson M, Weston C, Cunningham AD, Rickards AF, et al.. Improving care for patients with acute coronary syndromes: initial results from the National Audit of Myocardial Infarction Project (MINAP). Heart. 2004;90(9):1004-1009. doi:10.1136/hrt.2004.034470. PMID: 15310686.

audits.title: Thrombolysis in acute stroke: ongoing challenges based on a tertiary hospital audit and comparisons with other Australian studies.
audits.setting: Tertiary hospital stroke unit, Princess Alexandra Hospital, Queensland

cycle1.result: 57 of 490 ischaemic strokes (11.6%) received tPA; median onset to treatment 175 min; median door to needle 97 min; protocol deviations 21.1%

audits.other_findings: At 3 months 21.1% had died and 41.5% had favourable outcome; symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage 5.3%.
audits.citation: Lau AHT, Hall G, Scott IA, Williams M. Thrombolysis in acute stroke: ongoing challenges based on a tertiary hospital audit and comparisons with other Australian studies. Aust Health Rev. 2016;40(1):43-53. doi:10.1071/ah14167. PMID: 26117176.

audits.title: Success of audit in reducing the time taken to administer thrombolysis and aspirin in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
audits.standard: Local guidelines aimed at eliminating delays in thrombolysis and aspirin
audits.setting: Coronary care, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Median time to thrombolysis 55 min (21-148); time to ECG 14 min (4-34); time to start thrombolysis in CCU 15 min (0-110); time to aspirin 58 min (15-400).

audits.intervention: Sources of delay presented to clinical staff with guidelines aimed at eliminating delays.

cycle2.result: Median time to thrombolysis 38 min (15-155), a 31% reduction (P = 0.013); ECG 6 min (1-19) (P < 0.0001); CCU 10 min (5-70) (P = 0.047); aspirin 15 min (3-235) (P = 0.001).

audits.citation: Currie P, Gray SM, Shaw TR, Starkey IR. Success of audit in reducing the time taken to administer thrombolysis and aspirin in patients with acute myocardial infarction. Scott Med J. 1994;39(4):120-122. doi:10.1177/003693309403900409. PMID: 8778962.

audits.title: The use of audit to set up a thrombolysis programme in the accident and emergency department.
audits.standard: Door-to-needle time 30 min; 70% of acute myocardial infarction patients thrombolysed
audits.setting: Accident and emergency department, Gloucester Royal Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Median door-to-needle time 110 min; 58% of acute myocardial infarctions thrombolysed (thrombolysis run from coronary care unit).

audits.intervention: Thrombolysis programme moved from the coronary care unit to A&E, with funding for staffing and staff education.

cycle2.result: 266 (28%) had acute myocardial infarction; 182 (68%) received thrombolysis (vs 58% previously). Door-to-needle result truncated in abstract.

audits.other_findings: Audit data were used to obtain and then secure recurrent funding for the service.
audits.citation: Kendall JM, McCabe SE. The use of audit to set up a thrombolysis programme in the accident and emergency department. J Accid Emerg Med. 1996;13(1):49-53. doi:10.1136/emj.13.1.49. PMID: 8821229.

audits.title: Reducing thrombolytic therapy time delays in the emergency department.
audits.standard: Australian Council on Healthcare Standards guideline: thrombolysis within 60 min
audits.setting: Emergency department, Auburn Hospital (level 4 district hospital), Sydney

cycle1.result: 8 of 21 thrombolysed patients had a delay over 60 min after first ECG; median delay 55 min.

audits.intervention: ECG machine and alteplase kept in the emergency department, fax machine installed, staff education, and senior medical staff allowed to start treatment if consultant unavailable (April to September 1996).

cycle2.result: Median delay after first ECG reduced to 43 min.

audits.other_findings: Median time from chest pain onset to triage was 73 min.
audits.citation: Senior J, Patel N. Reducing thrombolytic therapy time delays in the emergency department. J Qual Clin Pract. 1998;18(2):99-107. PMID: 9631347.
